title: Bodyguard
hook: How does Bodyguard end? The suicide vest standoff, who really killed Julia Montague, and the bombmaker twist, explained in full.

sections.heading: Where the finale leaves David Budd
sections.body: By the final episode, PS David Budd, a Scottish Afghanistan veteran carrying untreated PTSD, is the prime suspect in the assassination of the Home Secretary he was assigned to protect. Julia Montague died from a bomb hidden beneath the stage at St Matthew's College, and Budd, who had grown close to her, is the convenient face for the crime. He is being framed by people inside the very institutions meant to investigate the attack. The finale strands him at his lowest, distrusted, surveilled and unstable, while the conspiracy that killed Montague works to make him the story's villain.

sections.heading: The suicide vest standoff
sections.body: The episode's centrepiece is a long, agonizing set piece. Budd is forced into a suicide vest rigged with a dead man's switch and walked through the streets while armed police train their weapons on him and bomb disposal officers try to defuse the device. The tension is built on the knowledge that one twitch ends him. His estranged wife, Vicky, runs toward him to stop the police shooting, and the standoff becomes the crucible where Budd has to prove he is a pawn, not the bomber. He survives the vest, and survival buys him the chance to chase the truth.

sections.heading: Who really did it
sections.body: The conspiracy unspools in layers. The bombmaker is Nadia Ali, the apparently frightened woman from the opening train sequence, who reveals she built the explosive devices herself and was paid to do so. Behind her is organized crime boss Luke Aikens, who wanted Montague dead because her surveillance legislation, RIPA-18, threatened his operations. His police insider is Chief Superintendent Lorraine Craddock, Budd's own commanding officer, who chose him as Montague's protection officer precisely because his troubled background made him the perfect fall guy. The frame was engineered from inside the police from the very start.

sections.heading: Resolution and thematic payoff
sections.body: Budd clears himself with the evidence he and Vicky assemble, including the kompromat material and proof he was set up. Aikens and Craddock are arrested, and Craddock confesses to leaking Montague's movements and enabling the assassination. The compromising files leak, toppling the Prime Minister and the Director-General of MI5. The series ends not on a triumph but on a quieter, more honest note. Budd finally admits he needs help and begins occupational therapy for his PTSD, and reconciles with his family. The man who spent six episodes protecting everyone else is allowed, at last, to be saved.

final_image: With the conspiracy exposed and his name cleared, Budd walks with his reconciled family toward treatment for his PTSD, the bodyguard finally letting himself be looked after.

lingering_questions.q: Who killed Julia Montague in Bodyguard?
lingering_questions.a: The bomb was built by Nadia Ali, who confesses she made the devices herself, and the assassination was ordered and paid for by crime boss Luke Aikens, with police insider Lorraine Craddock enabling it from inside the investigation.

No. He was deliberately framed. Lorraine Craddock chose him as Montague's protection officer because his PTSD and military background made him an ideal scapegoat, and he clears himself in the finale before the real conspirators are arrested.

lingering_questions.q: What does the leaked kompromat do?
lingering_questions.a: Once the compromising files are released, the fallout brings down the Prime Minister and the Director-General of MI5, exposing the corruption that surrounded Montague's death.
